manifest_repo_refs.refs_caveat: project-objects is the shared bare object database and has no refs of its own; the sibling repo project gitdir owns refs. Its packed-refs contains an older gitcode/master value 78e7835a3673fb41399c6c2f5e86c578530046a3, but the current loose gitcode/master ref overrides it and resolves to 7743. The newer scratch dsoftbus-source-pin-20261020 bare repo has no target object: Gitee master is ccb1a86..., GitHub yielded 0e0c18... as dangling, exact-SHA fetch attempts previously returned not our ref and a later GitHub attempt failed to connect. Do not conflate this scratch clone with the manifest-synced .repo refs/object database. No release tag points directly to 7743; the manifest revision and GitCode master ref are the pin evidence.

recovery.checkout_caveat: the component checkout's .git/config is unreadable in this Windows mount; refs were read from .repo/projects and object bytes from .repo/project-objects with GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY pointed at the shared object store. This did not write or replace the checkout.

peer_name_exposure.finding: ClientGetPeerSocketInfoById returns sessionNode->info.peerSessionName as PeerSocketInfo.name and peerDeviceId as networkId.
FillSessionInfoEx copies ChannelInfo.peerSessionName into the session record; this is the field later exposed by the public peer-info accessor.
Auth-channel JSON serializes DST_BUS_NAME and reads the remote SRC_BUS_NAME into peerData.sessionName.

After the auth-channel handshake callback, NotifyOpenAuthChannelSuccess places appInfo.peerData.sessionName in ChannelInfo.peerSessionName. It marks channelInfo.isEncrypt=false and uses a fixed AUTH_SESSION_KEY label; this alone does not settle whether the preceding auth transport authenticates/integrity-protects the name.
The peer session name is copied from the channel/session parameter into peerData.sessionName.

Open-channel JSON carries BUS_NAME/CLIENT_BUS_NAME and numeric UID/PID fields; corresponding parser paths read peer bus-name values. These excerpts do not show a comparison binding the UID/PID encoded in a DBinder service name to authenticated remote process credentials.

auth_transport_and_replay_observations.finding: AuthSessionHandleAuthFinish posts the FSM auth-finish event; this marks device-auth flow completion, not an explicit assertion that peer service-name UID/PID matches remote OS credentials.

AuthDataHead packs dataType/module/seq/flag/len and payload; receive code unpacks it and dispatches. Comm transport sequence is generated and used to derive direction. The inspected framing code does not itself demonstrate a freshness/replay rejection rule for the peer-name field; lower transport/auth handling and message-specific state must be audited before concluding replay or integrity properties.

identity_auth_integrity_replay_trace.bounded_verdict: Exact DSoftBus source provenance is recovered and all nine locally present files byte-match the target blobs. The reviewed path shows the peer session name crosses protocol parsing and is surfaced through PeerSocketInfo, but does not prove or disprove a cryptographic/OS-principal binding for the embedded UID/PID. Auth-channel transport integrity/replay semantics remain open. Do not promote DBINDER_ADD_COMMAUTH identity spoofability to a finding from this evidence alone.

candidate_status.existing_candidate: D27/T28 identity boundary follow-up (linked to the IPC DBINDER_ADD_COMMAUTH / service-name UID-PID path)
candidate_status.effect_of_new_evidence: source provenance blocker removed for DSoftBus 7743; manifest pins it alongside IPC 5903. Product build provenance, identity binding, auth-channel integrity/replay semantics, and the exact IPC 5903 pairing review remain unresolved.
candidate_status.second_layer_review_scope: Re-review only the recovered exact DSoftBus 7743 sources and frozen-manifest pair IPC 5903; keep as conditional/low-confidence until product build and peer-principal authentication/integrity evidence are established.

next_dependencies: Bind the frozen manifest pair (IPC 5903 + DSoftBus 7743) to a product build record or resolved GN dependency graph and artifact provenance.

Trace the exact auth-channel message send/receive and lower transport on each enabled link type; identify where integrity, encryption, peer-device authentication, and replay checks apply to SRC_BUS_NAME, and whether UID/PID is separately validated against the remote process principal.
Review the IPC 5903 source paths and verify they preserve the previously analyzed bbb92 behavior relevant to this candidate; do not infer pairing from a nearby but different IPC pin.
Only then decide whether to retain, reject, or promote the single consolidated identity-boundary candidate; no PoC, device test, or product build was run in D64.
